summary: Prospecta Health — EU regional streaming degradation causing truncated responses and elevated 5xx rate
description:
Issue summary:
Prospecta Health reported large numbers of truncated streaming responses and a spike in 5xx errors for requests routed to eu-west beginning 2026-02-26 12:45 UTC. Customers observed partial completions (stream closed mid-token) and increased client disconnects that affected chat and real-time note-generation features.

Impact:
- Affected ~120k requests over a 45-minute window for Prospecta Health (enterprise plan).
- Visible truncated completions for both text generation and function-calling flows.
- Increased retries from customer side led to elevated token counts and billing concerns.

Environment:
- Production (eu-west) serving nodes behind streaming-proxy cluster v2.11.
- Traffic routed to redwood-2.7b-v1 and open-llama-3b model variants.

Timeline (abridged):
- 12:45 UTC: First alert from synthetic monitors (stream-sanity-check) showing partial streams.
- 12:48 UTC: Prospecta Support slack #prospecta-support escalated to Redwood #support with examples.
- 12:50 UTC: SRE acknowledged and opened INC-2026-02-26-03.
- 13:10 UTC: Mitigation: temporarily route Prospecta traffic to warm fallback pool (higher latency but reliable).
- 13:24 UTC: Deploy of streaming-proxy hotfix (rollback of a kernel-selection optimization).
- 13:36 UTC: Observed complete recovery; monitoring returned to baseline by 13:55 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (customer report):
1) Initiate a streaming completion with prompt size ~1.2k tokens using redwood-2.7b-v1 pinned version.
2) Observe intermittent stream termination after ~30-60 tokens on eu-west hosts.
3) Repeating on dedicated capacity did not reproduce; issue was specific to shared eu-west pools.

Observed logs and traces (high level):
- streaming-proxy logs: repeated 'client_keepalive_timeout' and 'stream_flush_incomplete' entries correlated with kernel-selection events.
- serving-runtime traces: high rate of aborted KV-cache reconciliation when requests were migrated across worker threads during late-stage kernel swap.
- API gateway: 502/524 surge for streaming endpoints, 200s for single-request non-stream flows unchanged.

Current status: Resolved. Root-cause fix deployed and validated. Customer notified and billing anomaly under review.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: networking flaps between proxy and worker causing half-closed TCP leading to truncated streams — refuted by stable tcp-level metrics.
Telemetry review: spikes in 'kernel_swap' events coinciding with stream termination events and 'stream_flush_incomplete' errors logged by streaming-proxy (eu-west).
Reproduced in staging with traffic generator when kernel-selection optimization was enabled and worker thread migration occurred under load.

Root cause: a timing window during late-stage kernel selection where the streaming-proxy issued a flush while serving-runtime was migrating KV cache ownership; this could trigger partial chunk flushes and close stream before full completion. The optimization changed ordering of cache handoff and flush acknowledgement.

Evidence: correlated traces from trace-id 2026-02-26-1198 showing flush ack missing for final chunk, and subsequent proxy decision to close connection. Heatmap of events available in Grafana panel 'streaming/flush-latency/eu-west'.

Risk assessment: high for shared pools with high interleaved load and models with longer finalization sequences (e.g., redwood-2.7b-v1). Lower risk on dedicated pools, consistent with customer observations.
resolution: Immediate mitigation: route Prospecta Health traffic to the warm fallback pool for eu-west to prevent truncated streams (done 12:50 UTC).
Code fix: removed unsafe reordering in streaming-proxy related to kernel-selection flush timing and added an acknowledgement handshake (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/982).
Rollback/Deploy: rolled back optimization on streaming-proxy v2.11 and deployed patched v2.11.1 at 13:24 UTC; canary passed and cluster promoted at 13:32 UTC.

Monitoring: introduced new alert 'streaming.flush_ack_missing' and Grafana dashboard panel for flush/ack latency by region and model. Added 48h canary watch and 7-day trend retention for flush metrics.
Customer communication: initial incident notification within 30 minutes, full postmortem delivered 2026-02-28. Offered one-time billing credit and assistance in reducing client retry amplification.
